content: 1. Danicopan increases the plasma concentration of substrates of the breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). Dose reduction of BCRP substrates should be considered based on their prescribing information. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 3. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Ferrous fumarate reduces the levels of deferiprone by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Deferiprone may bind polyvalent cations (e.g., iron, aluminum, zinc); administration should be separated by at least 4 hours from antacids or supplements containing these cations. 6. Deferoxamine reduces the levels of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Deferoxamine chelates iron. 7. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels or effects of delafloxacin by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Oral delafloxacin forms chelate with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administer oral delafloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. 8. Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of diazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations of coadministered benzodiazepines. 11. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Administer dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after medications containing polyvalent cations. 13. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 14. Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Elafibranor, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce systemic exposure to hormonal contraceptives. Switching to effective nonhormonal contraceptives or adding a barrier method is recommended during elafibranor treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. 15. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitoring of CYP3A substrates is recommended, and dose adjustments may be necessary. 16. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 17. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Cobicistat, a CYP3A4 inhibitor, is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening events. 18. Encorafenib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Encorafenib may increase the concentration and toxicities of BCRP substrates. Close monitoring for signs of increased exposure and dose adjustments of these substrates are recommended. 19. Erythromycin base decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 20. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 21. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 22. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. 23. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. The use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 25. Ethinylestradiol may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide.
